# RQ2 — Immune-related signatures

Are 18-gene T-cell–inflamed GEP (see D6; Ayers et al. (2017)) associated with treatment response?<https://www.jci.org/articles/view/91190>

Reference: 10.1172/JCI91190

-   Suggested tasks: Identify the 18 genes included in the published T-cell–inflamed GEP and examine their expression in the dataset.

-   Calculate a T-cell–inflamed GEP score for each patient.

-   Investigate whether patients with higher GEP scores are more likely to respond to anti-PD-L1 treatment.

-   Interpret the biological significance of your findings and discuss why a high T-cell–inflamed GEP score does not necessarily guarantee treatment response

## Load packages

```{r}
packages <- c("immunedeconv", 
              "ggplot2",
              "limma",
              "tidyverse")
missing <- packages[!vapply(packages,
                            requireNamespace,
                            logical(1),
                            quietly=TRUE)]
if(length(missing)) 
  stop("Install missing packages: ",
       paste(missing,collapse=", "))

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(immunedeconv);
  library(ggplot2);
  library(limma);
  library(tidyverse)})
```

IMVigor <- readRDS("data/IMvigor210_plain.rds")

## Helper functions

```{r}
plot_response_boxplot <- function(data,variable,title) {
  ggplot(data,aes(x=Response,y=.data[[variable]])) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape=NA,alpha=.3) +
    geom_jitter(width=.12,alpha=.65,size=1.5) +
    labs(title=title,x="Response class",y=variable)+theme_minimal()
}
plot_association <- function(data,x,y,title) {
  ggplot(data,aes(x=.data[[x]],y=.data[[y]]))+
    geom_point(alpha=.7)+geom_smooth(method="lm",se=FALSE,color="steelblue")+
    labs(title=title,x=x,y=y)+theme_minimal()
}
spearman_test <- function(x,y) cor.test(x,y,method="spearman",exact=FALSE,use="complete.obs")
```

## Step 1 - Identify the 18 genes

```{r}
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rownames(counts)),
          all(colnames(counts) %in% rownames(clinical)))

gene_list <- rownames(counts)
```

```{r}
genes_18 <- c(
  "CD27", "CD274", "CCL5",
  "CD276", "CD8A", "CMKLR1",
  "CXCL9", "CXCR6", "HLA-DQA1", "HLA-DRB1", "HLA-E",
  "IDO1", "LAG3", "NKG7", "PDCD1LG2", "PSMB10", "STAT1", "TIGIT"
)

missing_GEP <- setdiff(genes_18, gene_list)
cat("GEP genes present:",
    length(genes_18)-length(missing_GEP),
    "of",length(genes_18),
    "\n")
if(length(missing_GEP))
  warning("Missing GEP genes: ",paste(missing_GEP,collapse=", "))
```

### Calculating GEP scores

```{r}
GEP_present <- intersect(genes_18, gene_list)

GEP_expr <- counts[GEP_present,,drop=FALSE]
# scale() standardizes columns, so transpose to standardize each gene across patients.
GEP_expr_scaled <- t(scale(t(GEP_expr)))
if(any(!is.finite(GEP_expr_scaled)))
  warning("Some gene z-scores are non-finite: check missing/constant genes")

GEP_scores <- colMeans(GEP_expr_scaled,na.rm=TRUE)
summary(GEP_scores)
```

## Step 2 - Creating the dataframe

```{r}
TMB <- clinical$TMB
PD1 <- as.numeric(counts["PDCD1",])
summary(TMB); summary(PD1)
```

```{r}
df <- data.frame(sample=colnames(counts),
                 TMB=TMB,
                 PD1=PD1,
                 GEP_scores=GEP_scores,
                 Response=factor(clinical$BOR))

table(df$Response)
```

## Step 3 - Analysis and Visualisation

### Wilcoxon tests

```{r}
if(nlevels(droplevels(df$Response))!=2) 
  stop("The supplied two-group Wilcoxon tests require exactly two response classes")

TMB_Response_test <- wilcox.test(TMB~Response,
                                 data=df,
                                 exact=FALSE)
PD1_Response_test <- wilcox.test(PD1~Response,
                                 data=df,
                                 exact=FALSE)
GEP_Response_test <- wilcox.test(GEP_scores~Response,
                                 data=df,
                                 exact=FALSE)

sapply(list(TMB=TMB_Response_test,
            PD1=PD1_Response_test,
            GEP=GEP_Response_test),
       function(x)x$p.value)
```

### Boxplot: T cell–inflamed GEP across response groups

```{r}
plot_response_boxplot(df,"GEP_scores","T cell–inflamed GEP across response groups")
```

```{r}
#| label: gep-response

# Wilcoxon test for GEP vs Response
GEP_Response_test <- wilcox.test(GEP_scores ~ BOR, data = clinical_filtered)

cat("\nWilcoxon test - GEP scores vs Response:\n")
print(GEP_Response_test)

# Identify outliers within each response class
outliers <- clinical_filtered %>%
  group_by(BOR) %>%
  filter(
    GEP_scores < quantile(GEP_scores, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) -
      1.5 * IQR(GEP_scores, na.rm = TRUE) |
    GEP_scores > quantile(GEP_scores, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) +
      1.5 * IQR(GEP_scores, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Boxplot
plot_response_boxplot(clinical_filtered, 
                      "GEP_scores",
                      "T cell-inflamed GEP score",
                      GEP_Response_test) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = outliers,
    aes(x = BOR, y = GEP_scores, label = Patient_ID),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    box.padding = 0.4,
    point.padding = 0.3
  )
```
